title: Bluevalve Therapeutics - renewal & geo expansion coordination
next_steps: Redwood to send updated SOW with EU on-prem line items
Bluevalve to share current token usage by route by 2026-09-17
Sophie to provision 72-hour EU private pilot (credentials + test prompts)
action_items: Maya Chen: Draft SOW addendum with EU on-prem and Dedicated burst pricing (due 2026-09-21)
Sophie Alvarez: Stand up 72-hour EU private pilot, provide access and run two benchmark prompts (due 2026-09-18)
Michael Grant: Share token-by-route usage CSV and current autoscaler settings (due 2026-09-17)
Priya Nair: Provide network contact for VPC peering and KMS questions (due 2026-09-16)
Samir Patel: Confirm procurement timeline and required PO terms (due 2026-09-23)
summary: Renewal check-in focused on adding EU on-prem pilot and modest capacity uplift. Customer emphasized data residency, KMS/HSM integration, and deterministic latency for clinical inference. Redwood to provide SOW addendum, stand up a 72-hour EU private pilot, and run latency/cost benchmark. Procurement expects decision by end of month; pilot results will inform contract amendment.
topics: EU on-prem pilot and data residency
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see Elena, Michael, Priya, Samir — thanks for making time. We'll do a quick agenda: renewal numbers, EU on-prem pilot, KMS + audit log questions, and next steps. Sophie and Liam are here from our side for technical and CS follow-up.
[00:18] Elena (Bluevalve CTO): Thanks Maya. Quick note: we're on a tight timeline on this quarter, so trying to align the pilot this month, yes.
[00:25] Michael (Head of Platform): Yup, timeline's tight. Also want to double-check our latency bounds. We're doing clinical triage inference; 95th percentile needs to be under 220ms for the short prompts.
[00:36] Sophie (Redwood SE): Sounds fair, we can run that. We'll need to know typical sequence lengths and batch patterns, but 220ms 95th is within scope on Dedicated with EU on‑prem — depending on model variant.
[00:48] Priya (DevOps): For the pilot we need VPC peering and KMS integration. Our security team will insist on customer-managed keys — HSM-backed if possible.
[00:58] Liam (CSM): Noted. Redwood supports external KMS/HSM via our Private deployment flow; Sophie can walk through the steps.
[01:06] Samir (Procurement): Also, what's the procurement window? I need to know when to expect a finalized SOW so we can route PO approvals.
[01:14] Maya: We'll aim to get an initial SOW addendum to you in three business days. That will include Dedicated pricing, on-prem pilot (72-hour), and EU capacity uplift options.
[01:24] Elena: Good. Can we talk about data residency — logs and retention? We need logs kept inside EU and audit trails for 12 months.
[01:33] Sophie: We can enable audit logs retained in the customer-controlled S3 in EU region. There are a couple of options: route logs to your bucket (preferred), or we keep logs and provide a retention SLA. Routing to your bucket gives you direct control.
[01:47] Michael: We'll prefer our bucket. Also must ensure PII redaction at ingest where possible; are there built-in redaction hooks?
[01:56] Sophie: We have pre-commit hooks (pre-processing) suggested patterns, but for strict PII removal we'd recommend pushing that as a pipeline step before calling the model. We can provide a reference lambda pattern.
[02:09] Elena: Okay. For the model itself, are you recommending a quantized variant to lower cost? Concern is quality drift.
[02:17] Sophie: For short clinical prompts you can often use an 8-bit quantized variant with negligible quality delta; our Optimize team ran a small eval — we can share results. For clinical, though, if you're risk-averse we can run a head-to-head in the pilot.
[02:30] Michael: That would be helpful. We need a perf vs quality matrix. Also the 95th latency target — can Redwood commit to fallback routes if the on-prem is saturated?
[02:40] Maya: Yes, we support smart routing. For customers on Private we can define a fallback policy to Hosted or Dedicated in other regions, but that affects residency guarantees. If residency is strict, fallback would only be to other EU private nodes.
[02:55] Priya: That raises a question — if fallback goes to another EU tenant, is data still within our control? We want to maintain isolation.
[03:03] Sophie: If we route to another EU private cluster owned by Bluevalve (i.e., additional nodes we provision in your VPC), isolation is maintained. If fallback uses our hosted cluster, that's a policy decision and requires consent.
[03:16] Samir: Procurement will want to see exact wording around that in the SOW — especially the fallback policy and SLA credits.
[03:23] Maya: We'll include precise fallback language and SLA credit clauses.
[03:27] Elena: On capacity numbers — we currently consume about 120M tokens/month, mostly embeddings and short chat completions. Peak concurrency is around 65 rps during clinical hours. We're asking for a 40% uplift to cover new workflows.
[03:42] Michael: I'll upload the token-by-route CSV after the call.
[03:45] Maya: Perfect. That helps sizing. Based on that uplift, we propose Dedicated pool with a small on-prem node pair in EU (two nodes) and burst capacity to double for 2-hour windows. We'll show the cost delta in the SOW.
[03:59] Priya: Two nodes — do you mean physical GPU hosts in our VPC or managed nodes in Redwood's private cluster in EU?
[04:08] Sophie: For Private we support both. In your case we recommend Redwood-managed Private cluster hosted in your cloud account (we provision EKS/GKE/GCP but nodes are in your tenant). That gives you network isolation and we manage runtime.
[04:20] Priya: Ok that is preferable. How does KMS handshake work then?
[04:25] Sophie: We support customer-managed KMS. The keys remain in your KMS; Redwood gets limited unwrap permissions via IAM role, and logs show key usage. For HSM specifically we can integrate — there are a few extra steps but it's supported.
[04:38] Michael: Sounds good. One technical ask — can we run warmup traffic to prepopulate KV caches before clinical hours? We need lower tail latency.
[04:47] Sophie: Yes, prewarming via automated warmup jobs is supported; we can include a job in the pilot that simulates morning load and warms KV caches.
[04:56] Maya: Great. Let's drill into pilot success criteria. What would Bluevalve consider a successful pilot?
[05:02] Elena: Success is: (1) 95th percentile latency < 220ms on our critical route during a 2-hour simulated window; (2) no data egress outside EU; (3) KMS integration validated with logs; (4) throughput matches predicted concurrency with no queueing.
[05:18] Sophie: We can define specific test prompts and run three repetitions across different model variants. We'll capture per-token latency, p95, and cost.
[05:27] Michael: Also include an accuracy / quality check vs our baseline model — we don't want quality regressions.
[05:33] Sophie: Understood. We'll include a small evaluation harness.
[05:37] Samir: On procurement — approval path for SOW typically takes two weeks internally, but if we have pilot results earlier we might fast-track.
[05:45] Maya: We'll get the SOW draft over ASAP. If pilot starts week of 9/21, results by 9/24 and procurement can aim the week after.
[05:54] Elena: One other question — do you provide SOC2 Type II artifacts and a data processing addendum? Security will ask for those.
[06:02] Liam: Yes we will share SOC2 report and DPA. I'll attach them to the follow-up email.
[06:07] Elena: Great.
[06:10] [06:10] Speaker 6: (inaudible)
[06:12] Maya: Quick operational detail — for the EU private pilot we'll need a small service account with limited IAM permissions. Priya, can you set that up or point us to your infra contact?
[06:22] Priya: I'll provide infra contact — Carmen in our cloud team. I'll email Carmen and cc Sophie.
[06:28] Sophie: Thanks. Also, what's your preferred times for the 72-hour pilot? We usually avoid Friday starts to avoid weekend support complications.
[06:36] Elena: Can we run Mon-Wed next week? That fits our security folks.
[06:40] Maya: Monday kickoff 2026-09-21 then. Sophie will provision Friday so you can smoke test overnight.
[06:47] Michael: One more thing — cost estimator. If we go Dedicated plus on-prem nodes, what's the expected uplift in monthly spend? Can you give a ballpark?
[06:56] Maya: Ballpark depending on model/quantization, a 40% token uplift plus Dedicated pool and two on-prem nodes would be roughly 60-80% increase in monthly committed spend versus current, but per-token unit cost could drop with Dedicated. We'll include modeled scenarios in the SOW.
[07:12] Elena: We need the per-route cost numbers; procurement cares about line-item granularity.
[07:18] Maya: We'll include per-route cost and a 'what-if' table for quantized vs full precision.
[07:23] [07:23] Michael: Any concerns with GDPR transfer? If everything stays in EU private nodes and logs in EU buckets, that should be fine.
[07:31] Sophie: Correct. We'll also include Data Processing Addendum with subprocessors list.
[07:36] Samir: For the PO — we prefer NET30 and a minor amendment to liability limits for clinical usage. Procurement will flag that.
[07:45] Maya: Noted. We'll talk to legal to see what flexibility exists on liability cap for this customer segment.
[07:52] Elena: Is there a chance to lock pricing if we commit to a 12-month Dedicated contract today?
[07:58] Maya: Yes, we offer commitment discounts for 12-month reserved vs month-to-month. We'll layout tiered pricing in SOW.
[08:06] Priya: Tech question — during the pilot will Redwood run benchmarks from inside our VPC or from outside?
[08:12] Sophie: Benchmarks will run from inside your VPC — we place probe instances to simulate real traffic. That gives you the most accurate numbers.
[08:19] Michael: Perfect.
[08:21] [08:21] Liam: Quick note — I'll follow up with SOC2, DPA, and the pilot runbook.
[08:27] Maya: Anything else?
[08:29] Elena: No, that's it for me. Looking forward to the SOW and pilot.
[08:33] Maya: Great. We'll recap action items in the follow-up and set the pilot kickoff meeting for 2026-09-21 09:00 CEST. Thanks everyone.
[08:41] [Crosstalk, people saying bye] 
[08:45] End of recording.
